headline: Sensex Trims Losses as Buying in PSU Banks and Reliance Offsets Private Bank Decline

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Sharp early losses were trimmed due to strong buying support in State Bank of India and Reliance Industries.
PSU bank stocks rallied up to 8% driven by positive Q2 earnings performance.
Private sector lenders including HDFC Bank and Axis Bank fell up to 5% post Q2 results, weighing on indices.
Elevated crude oil prices and weak Asian market cues created caution among investors.
whatHappening: PNB shares surged 8% after Q2 results exceeded market estimates, leading to target price upgrades by brokerages.
Sensex recovered over 300 points from its low after initially dropping over 500 points.
Jio Platforms announced its IPO opening date for October 21, with grey market premium pointing to potential listing gains.
Nifty IT index declined by 1% amid broader market volatility and global tech valuation concerns.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices trimmed sharp early losses as buying in heavyweights SBI and Reliance Industries provided support.
PSU banking stocks surged led by strong earnings beat from PNB, while private bank majors HDFC Bank and Axis Bank saw notable declines.
Investor sentiment remained cautious amid higher crude oil prices and mixed global market cues.
